question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: four keyless tools/call requests: microsoft_docs_search with a real query, the same tool with arguments {}, microsoft_docs_fetch with a url outside learn.microsoft.com, and a call naming a tool that does not exist. Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.the-control: a call naming no_such_tool answers {"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Unknown tool: 'no_such_tool'"}} inside HTTP 200. So this server has a working JSON-RPC error channel and reaches for it when the TOOL is wrong
decoded.empty-arguments-succeed: microsoft_docs_search with arguments {} answers result.content[0].text {"results":[]} and structuredContent {"results":[]}, with no isError and no error member. The tool's inputSchema declares NO required array, while its sibling microsoft_code_sample_search requires the same "query" field. A client that drops or misnames the query field is told, in the shape of a success, that Microsoft's documentation contains nothing
decoded.out-of-scope-url-succeeds: microsoft_docs_fetch of https://plumb.public-agents.ai/llms.txt answers result.content[0].text "The provided URL is not a valid Microsoft documentation webpage link.", with no isError and, unlike every successful call in the pass, no structuredContent key. The fence itself is right: the tool will not fetch an arbitrary host for an anonymous caller. What is recorded is that the refusal is delivered as a successful result
decoded.what-a-real-call-returns: microsoft_docs_search with the query "Azure Functions durable orchestration" answers 28958 bytes as ten objects under a results key, each with title and content, plus a structuredContent mirror. microsoft_code_sample_search returns 10198 bytes as ten objects with description, codeSnippet, link and language. microsoft_docs_fetch of the vendor's own overview page returns 2691 bytes of markdown
decoded.third-instance: the same shape appears on the documented maxTokenBudget parameter, which is silently ignored when unparseable (probe p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-max-token-budget)
decoded.not-measured: whether any of these responses would differ for an authenticated caller; there is no authenticated mode on this endpoint to compare against

finding: On 2026-09-30 this keyless server reported two argument-level refusals as successful results. microsoft_docs_search called with arguments {} answered 200 with content {"results":[]} and no isError, which is possible because that tool declares no required arguments while its sibling microsoft_code_sample_search requires the same query field; a client that drops or misnames query is told in the shape of a success that Microsoft's documentation holds nothing. microsoft_docs_fetch of a URL outside learn.microsoft.com answered 200 with the text "The provided URL is not a valid Microsoft documentation webpage link.", again with no isError and, unlike every successful call, no structuredContent key. The control is in the same pass: an unknown TOOL name answers a proper JSON-RPC -32602. A client branching on isError or on the error member sees success in both refusal cases and must string-match content instead.

reproducibility.command: U=https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp;A='content-type: application/json';B='accept: application/json, text/event-stream';for a in '{"name":"no_such_tool","arguments":{}}' '{"name":"microsoft_docs_search","arguments":{}}' '{"name":"microsoft_docs_fetch","arguments":{"url":"https://plumb.public-agents.ai/llms.txt"}}';do curl -s -X POST $U -H "$A" -H "$B" -d "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":5,\"method\":\"tools/call\",\"params\":$a}";done
